source_text: BEATRICE. For them all together; which maintained so politic a state of evil that they will not admit any good part to intermingle with them. But for which of my good parts did you first suffer love for me?
modern_text: BEATRICE. For them all together; which maintained so politic a state of evil that they will not admit any good part to intermingle with them. But for which of my good parts did you first suffer love for me?

source_text: DOGBERRY. Write down that they hope they serve God: and write God first; for God defend but God should go before such villains! Masters, it is proved already that you are little better than false knaves, and it will go near to be thought so shortly. How answer you for yourselves?
modern_text: DOGBERRY. Write down that they hope they serve God—and write God first; for God forbid that God should walk behind such villains! Masters, it is proved already that you are little better than false scoundrels, and it will go near to be thought so shortly. How do you answer for yourselves?

source_text: BEATRICE. Sadly, he gets nothing out of it. In our last clash, four of his five wits went limping off, and now the whole man is governed by just one. So if he has wit enough to keep himself warm, let him show it off as the only thing distinguishing him from his horse—because that's all the wealth he has left to be known as a reasonable creature. Who's his sidekick now? He swears a new brotherhood every month.
modern_text: BEATRICE. Alas! he gets nothing by that. In our last conflict four of his five wits went halting off, and now is the whole man governed with one! so that if he have wit enough to keep himself warm, let him bear it for a difference between himself and his horse; for it is all the wealth that he hath left to be known a reasonable creature. Who is his companion now? He hath every month a new sworn brother.
